title: Three Weeks and One Short Needle
subtitle: 仪表穿着 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）
meta: 主题语境：仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）　|　核心词汇：skirt　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 skirt 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1979 the tailor ① wore the skirt that no customer in the shop would have measured, and he said the wearing was the whole of the week. The ② skirt, meaning the garment itself and not the needle, ran three weeks and stayed unmeasured in the book; a skirt, he said, is the only thing in a shop that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ skirt in that shop had the same short needle beside it, and the ④ skirt at the far mirror, meaning the collar they kept for the children to mend and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A skirt, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the tailor said the measuring is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the skirt was the whole of the matter, meaning the grace and not the garment. The ⑥ skirt, meaning the grace and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; skirt, he said, is either something you wear or the only word that means both a garment and a grace. He said the grace is the part they remember.

By 1984 the ⑦ skirt had become a line in an order, and the order had become an argument about the short needle. The ⑧ skirt of the whole thing, the tailor wrote in November, was one shop and three weeks of measuring; skirt, he said, is either the collar at the far mirror or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ skirt I remember is the garment measured in the order, which closed in 1986 and is still measured as the quietest in the shop. A ⑩ skirt, my mother said in 1988, is the only garment that improves by being measured; every skirt, she said, is a grace that has agreed to look like a garment. She said the grace was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 裙子（指裁缝铺里每一条旁边的那一条）
B. n. 裙子（指那条裙子本身，与细细的针相对）
C. 固定搭配：wear the skirt 穿这一条裙子
D. n. 裙子（指留给孩子们补的那一道）
E. n. 裙子之事（抽象总称，指一处裁缝铺的裙子之事）
F. n. 裙子（指订单簿里写到、被测量的那一条）
G. n. 裙子、仪态（指一件事里人人都穿却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 仪态（抽象总称，指人人都穿却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: wear the skirt 意为“穿这一条裙子”，1979 年那位裁缝把裁缝铺里没有一位顾客肯测量的一条裙子做了一遍。
skirt 意为“裙子”，指那条裙子本身而不是细细的针，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被测量。
skirt 意为“裙子”，指裁缝铺里每一条旁边的那一条，每一条旁边都有同一枚细细的针。
skirt 意为“裙子”，指最远那面试衣镜的留给孩子们补的那一道，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
skirt 意为“裙子、仪态”，指一件事里人人都穿却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这条仪态就是那件事的全部。
skirt 意为“仪态”，指人人都穿却无人提起的那样东西而不是那条裙子，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
skirt 意为“裙子”，指订单簿里写到、被测量的那一条，到 1984 年这一条成了订单簿里的一行。
skirt 意为“裙子之事”，裁缝十一月写道，整件事的裙子之事是一处裁缝铺和三个星期的测量。
skirt 意为“裙子”，我记得的是订单簿里测量过的那一条，1986 年缝好了，至今仍被说成裁缝铺里最安静的一条。
skirt 为抽象总称，母亲 1988 年说，裙子是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的裙子。
